expected.why: 'It' is a payment platform that bolts identity onto Bitcoin payments (k35-38); after a clip about Bitcoin, the viewer hears that Bitcoin becomes pointless.

sentences.text: So when I lost it, I went to buy it again, right?
And at the time, they accepted Bitcoin as payment.
and I went to pay for it, and I don't remember exactly what it did, but I couldn't get it to give me a Bitcoin address.

It gave me like use Binance wallet or Coinbase wallet or Metamask, and each of these required me to set up some sort of K -Y -C account with some fucking company that will only open a link to the relevant application that I would have to have installed and be signed in with my identity connected to it.
It would not give me a Bitcoin address to pay with.
because it doesn't actually respect the underlying neutrality of the protocol.
Where have you ever heard a Bitcoin complain about that?
Twitter is our town square.
That is where most of the majority around what happens on Bitcoin occurs in the world.
It happens on Twitter.
I'm not saying there aren't hundreds of other venues for it, but I'm pretty sure that is the most important one.
It accepts Bitcoin, except it doesn't... allow us to actually pay each other in a peer -to -peer way.
It requires permission.

It's done it in a way that undermines the entire point of it, the peer -to -peer payment network aspect of it, the fact that I can pay any address, as long as there's a valid address, I can pay it, and I can pay it from any valid UTXO.
That is undermined by enforcing a system on top of it that says, no, we need your identity to be attached to your activity somehow.
It becomes completely pointless.
There is no difference between making payments that way and making payments with a credit card.
It's the same system.
You haven't escaped Fiat at all.
All you've done is escape inflation by being involved in Bitcoin at that point.
You haven't... freed yourself from the tyranny of regulated payment networks, which was one of the main points.
There are two points to Bitcoin.
There's a disinflationary currency that allows you to store value and not lose it and store your work and labor over long periods of time.
That's half of it.
The other half of it is I can make payments to anyone, anywhere, and no one can stop me.
That's the other half of it.
And the Bip -110ers and the XBT heads and all those, we have spoken about how the second aspect can be undermined with centralized mining and top -down soft forks and things like that.
And I really want to stress that all of that can be true, but this is already gone.
It's already a thing that's not there anymore.
It's not just X premium.
